sectionsContent.title: Vectors & Vector Basics — Draw & Describe

concept.summary: A vector is a quantity with both magnitude and direction, drawn as an arrow. Section A practices drawing vectors tip-to-tail — the construction skill everything later in this unit is built on. Section B practices describing one vector's direction the other equivalent ways you'll need throughout this unit.
keyIdeas: Tip-to-tail: each new vector's tail starts exactly at the arrowhead of the one before it.
Every direction can be written three equivalent ways: a positive course angle, its negative form, or a compass phrase.
A compass phrase has two valid phrasings for the same direction — they always add to 90°.

items: Measuring an angle with a protractor, and plotting a point from an x–y coordinate (U0 S0.4).
A scalar is magnitude only; a vector adds direction to that.

sectionsContent.directions: Section A: draw each set of vectors tip-to-tail, in the order given, starting at the dot. Section B: using the reference circle, write each vector's other two correct descriptions.

equations.plain: Tip-to-tail: vector 2 starts exactly where vector 1's arrowhead ends
Positive course angle: counterclockwise from East, 0° to 360°
Negative course angle = positive course angle − 360°
